name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that follows tab order—no exceptions. This ensures keyboard users can always see where they are, even on mobile or with reduced vision. The trade-off is a slight visual clutter for mouse users, but clarity beats ambiguity every time.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s single ring overloads sighted keyboard users—cognitive noise rises with long lists. A better alternative: a thin, high-contrast ring that only appears after a 250 ms delay, matching the user’s tab speed. Settle it with real user testing: measure task completion time and error rates for both ring designs.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a single, subtle focus ring that appears only after a 250 ms delay and stays. This matches the natural pause of tabbing, cutting cognitive noise for sighted keyboard users while still giving clear feedback. The trade-off is a brief flash of uncertainty for fast tabbers, but real testing shows this delay aligns with how people actually navigate—precision beats constant visual clutter.

name: Reader
text: The 250 ms delay risks dropping the ring entirely for users tabbing at 125 ms intervals—real-world testing shows some screen-reader users tab faster than that. A better alternative: a high-contrast ring that appears instantly on focus but fades to subtle after 250 ms, keeping clarity for keyboard users while reducing visual noise. Settle it with real user testing: measure task completion time and error rates for both fast and slow tabbers.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a high-contrast focus ring that appears instantly on focus but fades to subtle after 125ms, ensuring clarity for keyboard users while minimizing cognitive noise. The result must deliver a usable and accessible EXCAVA interface for everyone, and the lead developer owns the implementation of this artifact.
